name: Refureku
listed_description: A C++17 runtime reflection and code generation library.
reason: README, Docs folder (Doxyfile and logos only) and issues searched: no benchmark, no numbers, no performance claim. A WebSearch for Refureku vs RTTR benchmarks found nothing. 253 stars, MIT.

name: RTTR
reason: Repo ships src/benchmarks (bench_method, bench_rttr_cast, bench_variant; nonius harness, rttr_cast vs dynamic_cast style cast test classes) but no results are checked in and the README only says it 'contains a faster' replacement for RTTI without numbers or a named baseline. Release notes 0.9.5/0.9.6 only say benchmarks were added. rttr.org and the 2015 habr.com comparison are egress-blocked; the habr snippet shows RTTR invoke at 1000 ms and 1135 ms with find+invoke, as the slower side. No numeric win over a named baseline reachable.

name: simpleini
listed_description: Cross-platform C++ library providing a simple API to read and write INI-style configuration files.
reason: README has no performance claim or benchmark; searched for third-party INI parser shootouts (inih, minIni, mINI, iniparser) and found none that include it. Only an opinion that it is heavy template code (benhoyt.com inih post snippet).

name: TinyXML
listed_description: A simple, small, minimal, C++ XML parser that can be easily integrating into other programs.
reason: SourceForge page has no speed comparison and says development moved to TinyXML-2. Third-party XML benchmarks (pugixml benchmark page, rapidxml, bemayer/xml-benchmark which excludes it) show TinyXML as the slow baseline, not a winner; tinyxml2 issue #52 holds no numbers. No claim of beating a named baseline.

name: TinyXML++
listed_description: A completely new interface to TinyXML that uses MANY of the C++ strengths. Templates, exceptions, and much better error handling.
reason: Wrapper interface over TinyXML; 728-byte README, no benchmark and no performance claim. Also folds into TinyXML as a wrapper.

name: toml11
listed_description: a C++11 (or later) header-only toml parser/encoder depending only on C++ standard library.
reason: No claim of beating another library. Only numeric data: release 4.4.0 'Improve toml::parse performance by 2x' (against its own earlier version) and open PR #320 (~4x vs its own original, i5-12600KF, 122-line config, 10000 parses), where toml++ stays 3.8x-4.8x faster (1178.6 ms vs 4482.6 ms). leptris/teptris benchmarks/LEDGER.md (M1 Max, -O3 -DNDEBUG -flto=thin) puts toml11 v4.2.0 slowest of six C/C++ TOML parsers by 17x to 430x vs toml++. Documented as slower than toml++, no win. Candidate for a not-faster keep entry if the orchestrator wants one.
